findings.verdict_note: All cites verified: 16x16 scrubber thumb on 4px track (style.css:153-168), #scrubber-close 22x22 (124-127), 14x14 setting checkmarks (230-231), 12px settings range thumb on 3px track (282-292), only #settings-btn gets a mobile 44px override (1083-1086), tour dots 6x6 with click handler (tour.css:317-326, tour.js:110 — they are spans, not <button>, a trivial detail), #tour-close 24x24 (tour.css:107-124), .search-item 6px padding/11px font ≈ 26-28px rows (470-472).

dimensions.summary: The startup path is desktop-shaped and hits a mid-range phone three times at once: nothing paints until the entire 360KB (114KB gz) bundle executes and builds the scene twice (body is opacity-gated until the module's last line), the boot then immediately plays a 3-second zoom animation that tears down and rebuilds the whole SVG DOM — including ~360 stroked text nodes — every frame, and module evaluation simultaneously fires ~260 network requests (130 icon chunks + ~1.2MB of webp, despite a comment claiming ~70KB). A permanent rAF loop with per-frame feGaussianBlur dots keeps the CPU/GPU busy forever afterward. KaTeX is already correctly code-split and the tile pyramid is small and well-leveled, so the fixes are mostly about deferral, batching icons, un-gating first paint, and adding a service worker for repeat visits — not re-architecting.

findings.title: First paint is gated on executing the entire 360KB main bundle (blank screen; blank forever on JS error)
findings.evidence: index.html:21-25 inlines `body:not(.ready){opacity:0!important}` and the only thing that adds `.ready` is `document.body.classList.add("ready")` at the very last line (5621) of the 5,621-line module. Before that line runs, the module synchronously: parses/executes dist/assets/index-DaavPvX1.js (360,162 B raw / 114,212 B gzip), builds the full SVG scene, and fires the initial zoom transform at line 5603 (`svg.call(zoomBehavior.transform, ...)` at k=14), which synchronously invokes the zoom 'end' handler's full redraw() (line 4628) — a second complete scene build. dist/index.html has no preload hints beyond the fonts preconnect. If any exception is thrown mid-module, `.ready` never fires and the page is permanently invisible.
findings.mobile_impact: On a ~4x-slower CPU, 360KB of JS parse+execute plus two full D3 scene constructions is easily 1.5-3s of main-thread work stacked on top of the 4G fetch of a 114KB gzip bundle — during which the user sees literally nothing, not even the static HTML chrome (title, buttons, search box) that is already parsed. Older Android browsers that throw on any newer syntax get a permanent black page.
findings.fix: Gate only #chart behind `.ready` (or use a skeleton/splash), let the static HTML UI paint immediately, add a `setTimeout` fallback that adds `.ready` after ~3s, and move `document.body.classList.add("ready")` before the boot section (or wrap boot in try/finally). Longer term, split the module so first paint needs only scaffolding + one render.
findings.verdict_note: Verified: index.html:21-25 inlines body:not(.ready){opacity:0!important}; main.js is exactly 5,621 lines and document.body.classList.add("ready") is the literal last line (5621) with no try/finally or timeout fallback, so any module-eval exception leaves the page permanently invisible. Bundle sizes are exact (dist/assets/index-DaavPvX1.js = 360,162 B raw, 114,212 B gzip). dist/index.html has only the two fonts preconnects — no preload/modulepreload. Line 5603 svg.call(zoomBehavior.transform, ...) synchronously emits start/zoom/end, and the end handler (main.js:4628) calls the full redraw(). One nit: I found no earlier top-level full scene build during module eval (only scaffolding/defs), so this transform-triggered redraw appears to be the FIRST full build, not a 'second' one — the zoom handler's rAF light-redraw is skipped because _zooming is false by then (main.js:4605). That detail overstates the work slightly but does not change the finding.

findings.title: Boot intro animation runs 3 seconds of full SVG DOM teardown/rebuild every frame
findings.evidence: Lines 5598-5611: unconditionally (mobile included) the app starts at k=14 and runs a 3000ms d3 transition to k=1. Every rAF frame the zoom handler calls redrawVectorsLight() (line 4617), which invokes 15 draw functions that each do `selectAll("*").remove()` + full rebuild (20+ teardown sites: lines 553, 661, 763, 915, 1237, 1361, 1477, 1713, 1785-1787, 3293, 3318, 3775...). drawObjects alone rebuilds ~180 objects with per-object closures (lines 2239-2267) and appends TWO stroked `<text>` nodes per object — halo stroke-width:3 + fill (lines 2217-2236) — even for labels that are `display:none`, i.e. ~360 text nodes per frame, plus O(n²) clustering BFS (1856-1871).
findings.mobile_impact: Rebuilding hundreds of SVG nodes (including stroked, letter-spaced text rasterized at DPR~3) per frame is 50-150ms/frame on a mid-range Android → the very first thing a mobile user experiences is a ~7-15fps janky 3-second animation, exactly matching the 'slow/janky animations' complaint. It also overlaps the icon/tile/font network burst.
findings.fix: On mobile (or always), skip the intro transition or run it as a CSS/attribute transform of the already-rendered `lContent` group (the code already does exactly this for tiles at lines 4607-4614), doing one full render at the end. Independently: don't append label text nodes whose display is 'none', and attach hover handlers only on non-touch devices.
findings.verdict_note: Verified: main.js:5598-5611 has no mobile guard — intro starts at k=14 and runs a 3000ms d3 transition to identity whenever there is no URL hash. The zoom handler (4600-4620) rAF-throttles to one redrawVectorsLight() per frame (4617), which calls 15 draw/update functions (4546-4569); all cited selectAll("*").remove() teardown sites exist at 553, 661, 763, 915, 1237, 1361, 1477, 1713, 1785-1787, 3293, 3318, 3775. drawObjects appends TWO stroked <text> nodes per rendered object (halo stroke-width 3 at 2217-2226 + fill at 2228-2236) even when labelDisplay is "none" (2216), plus per-object mouseenter/mouseleave closures (2239-2267), and runs the O(n²) BFS clustering at 1856-1871. objects.json has exactly 180 objects. Nit: labels are appended only for on-viewport objects with _showDot=true (1818-1823, 2163), so '~360 text nodes per frame' is the end-of-zoom-out figure; early intro frames build fewer. The tiles-CSS-transform precedent at 4607-4614 is real. Note the comment at 4558-4563 (backed by user memory) forbids swapping in the dots-only fast renderer during zoom — any fix must keep labels rendered.

findings.title: All 130 icons eagerly fetched at module load: ~260 requests / 1.2MB, not the claimed ~70KB
findings.evidence: Line 94: `Promise.all(Object.keys(ICON_BY_SLUG).map(s => getIconUrl(s)))` fires a dynamic import for every icon at module evaluation. The comment on line 93 says '~70KB total' but content/icons/*.webp is 1.2MB across 130 files. Each import.meta.glob entry is its own chunk: dist/assets holds 244 tiny non-index JS files totaling 169,441 B; 40 of them embed base64 data URIs (+33% size), the rest chain a second request for the .webp. When all resolve it triggers yet another full redraw() (line 95).

findings.title: Connection-dot animation runs an unstoppable requestAnimationFrame loop from boot, with per-frame SVG blur filters
findings.evidence: initConnections() (called at boot, line 5575) starts animateConnections at line 3771; the loop (3908-3997) unconditionally re-queues itself every frame forever — even when `_animPaused` or `_animDisabled` it still runs and re-queues (3917-3922, 3997). data.js defines 186 dots across 19 paths; each dot renders CLUSTER_DOTS=5 circles (up to 930 elements) with ~5 setAttribute calls per circle per frame, and head dots get `filter="url(#conn-glow)"` (line 3936), an feGaussianBlur (lines 453-459) re-rasterized every frame.
findings.mobile_impact: The page never goes idle: continuous rAF work burns battery and steals frame budget from pinch-zoom/pan on a weak CPU, and per-frame feGaussianBlur rasterization is brutal on a fill-rate-bound mobile GPU. This runs even when zero connection paths are visible at the current zoom.
findings.fix: Cancel the rAF (don't re-queue) when no `cp._visible` path exists, when `_animDisabled`, or when document.hidden; restart it from drawConnections()/visibilitychange. Replace the feGaussianBlur on animated dots with a pre-blurred radial-gradient fill. Consider disabling the animation entirely below a viewport-width threshold.
findings.verdict_note: Verified: initConnections() called at boot (main.js:5575) starts the rAF at 3771; animateConnections (3908-3997) re-queues itself unconditionally at 3910, 3921 and 3997 — including when _animDisabled (3917-3922). When _animPaused only dot advancement stops (3946); the per-dot setAttribute loop (3958-3995: cx, cy, r, fill, opacity per circle) still runs every frame, and applyEmWave uses the timestamp so positions keep changing. data.js has exactly 19 dotCount entries totaling 186 dots; CLUSTER_DOTS=5 (3714) → up to 930 circles. Head dots of spectrum/evolution paths get filter=url(#conn-glow) (3936), an feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 2 with 400% filter region defined at 453-459, re-rasterized as cx/cy change each frame. findings.title: Render-blocking third-party Google Fonts CSS loading 7 font faces
findings.evidence: Line 20 loads fonts.googleapis.com/css2 with Inter 300;400;500;600;700 + Space Mono 400;700 as a plain render-blocking stylesheet (same in dist/index.html:20).
